Let me preface this with I have never played any of the original 3 dead space titles. I saw this was on sale and decided to give it a go. The game was enjoyable, yet repetitive. Go here, this is broken, fix it, unlock the tram, head to next area rinse/repeat. By the end of the game I just wanted it to be over. The performance and graphics of the game were great, and sound design was pretty good, except sometimes the characters speaking felt a little to low to hear while everything else was loud. Story was OK if a bit generic and the ending while leaving it open ended, offered no real resolution or info for the main character. I felt a little underwhelmed after having just gone through the resident evil series.

Yeah, It's pretty much a perfect remake of an already perfect game. If you ever want to get into game design, study this one for a bit. They did just about everything right.

In order to make something right you have to make it at least twice. Or in this case in order to make something perfect. This remake takes one of the most enjoyable and well designed games ever made and removes the handful of negatives in favour of the better designs of the sequel. The graphics are awesome and the weapon upgrade path has been improved. Everything is better except for a few minor story moments with Hammond and Chen which arguably aren't changed for the better. The game play, atmosphere, graphics, and sound are pure perfection. The New Game+ is also a very welcome addition that made me play a second run immediately after my first.

Overall I've been really loving this game I recently had been playing the OG 2008 game on my steam deck and its been a blast with how well the classic has really held up. This feels like they legit were fans of the first two games and put their hearts into it. Everything you remember is roughly there that was a triggered event and looks beautiful, The gameplay feel is a nice blend between the first and second games. Isaac overall moves faster then originally but so do the necromorphs hell I had one slasher sprint and then leap to get me! everything in the game has serious weight when it comes to the sound design as they did an amazing job. Isaac's footsteps or hearing his heart when a spooky thing or from a fight, The power behind the weapons we use and the overall amazing atmosphere. Also love the new mechanic in certain areas where you have the choice of what to give up to progress the objective, will you run back with no lights except for emergency ones or will you try to speed run it with no life support so your on a timer.

Its a good graphical and Mechanics based remake that does well rebalancing weapons ,encounters, and set pieces, improving an all of these. fleshes out characters like Isaac and Nichole, and tries to expand upon the narrative but does fumble abit, the new actors and character design for Hammond and Klien feel much weaker than in the original, and not every new change to improved the narrative is taken to it's full potental, and does also have moments of graphical glitches, I wish Motive got to Create another Dead Space project after this because I wanted to see them take the lessons they learned from this game and use it to develop something better in the future.

Original game still feels good, but this overhaul makes it better by improving the game with features learnt and developed through the evolution of the Dead Space series, as well as the gaming industry.

Isaac now has voice and rewritten script takes this into consideration, making characters interact on a whole new level comparing to the original game, where our main character was basically a speechless machine. Moreover the USG Ishimura spaceship was made WHOLE by connecting and intertwining all ship sections and rooms into one amazing maze full of Dead Space atmosphere and with no loading screens...

Altogether now it's the best point to enter this amazing universe of Unitology, Sci-Fi and Survival Horror.

This is a great and honest remake. everything from the way you move and traverse throughout the Isimura, to the navigation the area and weapons through combat are greatly improved. I can only imagine that this is what the original team wanted when they made org. Dead Space. I'm glad to have seen this come out and wish there was a remake for 2.

Though plagued with some stuttering and general performance issues, this is a new gold standard for remakes, standing proudly along with the original if not surpassing it. They have taken what we know about the tale aboard the Ishimura and haven't just emulated it well, but they've elaborated on the plot strings left behind, tastefully introduced enhancements from the future entries to the series, and tweaked the whole experience just enough so it feels fresh and exciting.

Although we lament the loss of Visceral Games, it is clear that Motive understands the series well, and I am confident it is in good hands. I look forward to not only potential remakes of the other entries to the series, but any original projects we may get from Motive!
